_comment: Word list used by moderation.service.js to flag outgoing agent messages — no AI/API involved, so this list is the ONLY thing controlling what gets caught. Edit freely: add/remove words, redeploy, done. 'severe' = clear profanity/insults/threats, plus rude 1st/2nd-person pronouns (มึง/กู/etc) toward a customer — unacceptable in a sales/service role even without another swear word attached. 'minor' = dismissive/unprofessional tone that falls short of that. Entries here are written with no spaces (spaces are stripped before matching either way). Thai entries are matched against Wordcut-segmented tokens — a hit only counts if it's boundary-aligned (not sitting in the middle of a longer real word), so 'กู' no longer matches inside 'กู้เงิน'/'กู้คืน', 'บ้า' no longer matches inside 'บ้าง'/'บ้าน', etc. — see moderation.service.js and scripts/test-moderation.js for the mechanism and the regression suite. English entries still use plain substring matching (English already has space-delimited words, and none of these are short/common enough to plausibly nest inside an innocent English word here). Known residual gap: a handful of harsh-but-not-identical compound words that Wordcut's dictionary treats as their own single token (e.g. 'เหี้ยม' ruthless, distinct from 'เหี้ย') won't trigger a hit even though they're in the same spirit — add them here explicitly by name if they turn out to matter in practice, the same way 'โง่เขลา' was added alongside 'โง่'.
